title: Colonoscopy screening and smoking cessation - a teachable moment?
summary: The aim of the study is, on the one hand, to identify the needs and support options of smokers who do a colorectal cancer screening. On the other hand, colorectal cancer screening is explored as a possible teachable moment for quitting smoking and the impact of screening on motivation to quit will be investigated. For this purpose, smokers who either attend a colonoscopy screening or a GP appointment will be assessed. At two measurement points (before the screening/appointment and one month after the screening/appointment), smoking behavior, motivation to stop smoking, beliefs about factors influencing the risk of colorectal cancer and compensatory health beliefs are measured in both groups. These are beliefs that negative consequences of unhealthy behaviors can be compensated for by other healthy behaviors and it is investigated whether these have an (additional) influence on the motivation to stop smoking.
conditions: We investigate the smoking behavior of active smokers and their motivation to stop smoking in the context of colorectal cancer screening.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Active smoker
Participation in a colonoscopy for colorectal cancer screening, no medical indication (in the group of smokers with colonoscopy)
Exclusion criteria:
Participation in a colonoscopy screening within the last 12 months (in the group of smokers without a colonoscopy)
Insufficient German language skills
